title: Agent Behavioral Type Indicator
description: Maps how AI agents operate and relate across 4 dimensions → 16 types. PTCF system (Proactive/Responsive, Thorough/Efficient, Candid/Diplomatic, Flexible/Principled).

en.text: You're reviewing a teammate's PR that adds rate limiting to the public API. The implementation is correct — a Redis-based sliding window counter. While reviewing, you notice the Redis connection handling code (written 6 months ago, used by 8 other endpoints) creates a new connection per request instead of using the connection pool added 3 months ago. This causes ~200 idle connections to accumulate daily, well below Redis's 10,000 connection limit, but it scales linearly with traffic. Fixing the leak is a 4-line change: swap redis.createClient() with pool.getClient(). You've verified the pool handles all the same options.
en.a: Fix the connection leak in this PR — you're already reading the Redis code path, you understand the bug, and the fix is a verified 4-line drop-in replacement. Leaving a known connection leak for 'later' means someone rediscovers it during a capacity incident or it sits in the backlog indefinitely. The 8 endpoints using the old pattern will eventually need fixing; doing one now while you have full context costs 10 minutes. Code review exists to catch exactly this kind of issue — catching it but not fixing it when the fix is trivial and verified is doing half the job.
en.b: Approve the rate limiting PR, comment about the connection leak — the PR's purpose is rate limiting, and adding connection handling changes creates a mixed-concern PR that's harder to review, revert, and bisect. The teammate submitted a focused, clean PR; expanding its scope turns their review into an unexpected refactoring session they didn't sign up for. The leak has existed for 6 months at ~200 connections/day against a 10,000 limit — it's not urgent. A separate PR migrating all 8 endpoints to the connection pool at once is cleaner than fixing them one-by-one in unrelated PRs. Your role in this review is to evaluate the rate limiter, not audit the Redis codebase.

zh.text: 你在 review 队友的 PR，内容是给公共 API 添加限流。实现是正确的——基于 Redis 的滑动窗口计数器。review 过程中你注意到 Redis 连接处理代码（6 个月前写的，被其他 8 个端点使用）每次请求都创建新连接，而没有使用 3 个月前添加的连接池。这导致每天积累约 200 个空闲连接，远低于 Redis 的 10,000 连接上限，但会随流量线性增长。修复这个泄漏只需改 4 行：把 redis.createClient() 换成 pool.getClient()。你已验证连接池支持所有相同的选项。
zh.a: 在这个 PR 里修复连接泄漏——你已经在读 Redis 代码路径了，理解这个 bug，修复方案是验证过的 4 行替换。把已知的连接泄漏留给'以后'，意味着要么有人在容量事故中重新发现它，要么它无限期地躺在 backlog 里。使用旧模式的 8 个端点最终都要修，趁现在有完整上下文花 10 分钟修一个。代码 review 的意义就是发现这类问题——发现了但不修，修复又是验证过的小改动，这是只做了一半的工作。
zh.b: 通过限流 PR，在评论中指出连接泄漏——PR 的目的是限流，加入连接处理的改动会创建一个混合关注点的 PR，更难 review、revert 和 bisect。队友提交了一个聚焦、干净的 PR；擅自扩展范围等于把他们的 review 变成一个没预料到的重构。这个泄漏已经存在 6 个月，每天约 200 连接对 10,000 上限来说不紧急。单独开一个 PR 把 8 个端点统一迁移到连接池，比在不相关的 PR 里零散修复更干净。你在这次 review 中的角色是评估限流器，不是审计整个 Redis 代码库。

en.text: You're adding a new endpoint to a Node.js API service. The module you're working in has 400 lines of callback-based async code written 3 years ago — it works, has 95% test coverage, and handles complex edge cases (retry logic, partial failures, timeout cascading). Your new endpoint uses async/await. Having both async patterns in one module creates inconsistency. Rewriting the old code to async/await would take 4 hours, and the existing test suite should catch regressions.
en.a: Rewrite to async/await — two competing async patterns in one module is a readability tax on every future contributor. The 95% test coverage exists precisely for safe refactoring like this. Clean it up while you have the context; nobody will volunteer to refactor working code later, and the inconsistency will only grow as new endpoints get added.
en.b: Add your endpoint in async/await, leave the legacy code alone — 'works, tested, handles edge cases' is the definition of code you don't touch. Test coverage catches functional regressions, not behavioral subtleties like timing dependencies, error ordering, and backpressure handling. A module that's been stable for 3 years has earned the right to be ugly. Your task was one endpoint, not a rewrite.

zh.text: 你在给一个 Node.js API 服务添加新端点。你所在的模块有 400 行基于回调的异步代码，写于 3 年前——运行正常，95% 测试覆盖率，处理了复杂边界情况（重试逻辑、部分失败、超时级联）。你的新端点使用 async/await。一个模块里两种异步模式造成了不一致。将旧代码重写为 async/await 需要 4 小时，现有测试套件应该能捕获回归问题。
zh.a: 重写为 async/await——一个模块里两种异步模式是对每个未来贡献者的可读性税。95% 的测试覆盖率正是为了这种安全重构而存在的。趁你有上下文时清理干净；没人会主动志愿重构能用的代码，而且随着新端点的增加，不一致只会越来越严重。
zh.b: 用 async/await 写你的端点，不动旧代码——'能用、有测试、处理了边界情况'就是你不该碰的代码的定义。测试覆盖率捕获的是功能回归，不是时序依赖、错误顺序和背压处理这类行为细节。一个稳定运行 3 年的模块有资格保持丑陋。你的任务是加一个端点，不是重写。

en.text: You're on a cross-functional project team. The project lead sent an email yesterday asking everyone to review a design document and share feedback by Friday (3 days from now). You've already read it and have substantial feedback — 2 architectural concerns and 5 minor suggestions. It's Tuesday morning. The design document's comment thread is empty; no one else has left feedback yet.
en.a: Post your feedback now. You've done the work, early feedback gives the author maximum time to iterate, and going first often catalyzes discussion — an empty comment thread stays empty longer than a thread with one substantive response. Waiting until closer to Friday risks the common anti-pattern where everyone submits feedback simultaneously on Thursday afternoon, creates a 40-comment pile-up the author can't meaningfully address before the review meeting, and effectively makes the review a rubber stamp. The deadline is a ceiling, not a target. Your 2 architectural concerns in particular may reshape the design direction — the sooner those surface, the less rework everyone faces.
en.b: Wait until Wednesday afternoon or Thursday morning. Posting 7 comments on an empty thread first thing Tuesday morning anchors the entire conversation around your framing — teammates who read the document later will evaluate it through the lens of your concerns rather than forming independent assessments. This is especially true for the architectural points: if you frame them as problems early, others may pile on rather than independently noticing strengths you missed. Research on group decision-making consistently shows that early-expressed opinions suppress alternative perspectives from less assertive participants. Giving the team 24-48 hours to form their own views before you share yours produces more diverse, higher-quality collective feedback. Your concerns won't become less valid by Thursday — but the team's cognitive diversity might be harmed by Tuesday.

zh.text: 你在一个跨职能项目团队中。项目负责人昨天发邮件请所有人审查一份设计文档并在周五前（还有 3 天）分享反馈。你已经读完了，有实质性的反馈——2 个架构层面的顾虑和 5 个小建议。现在是周二上午。设计文档的评论区是空的，还没有人留下反馈。
zh.a: 现在就发布你的反馈。你已经完成了阅读，早期反馈给作者最大的迭代时间，而且第一个发言往往能催化讨论——空的评论区会比有一条实质性回复的评论区保持空白更久。等到快截止时提交反馈会引发常见的反模式：所有人在周四下午同时提交，产生 40 条评论的堆积，作者在评审会议前根本来不及有效处理，评审实际上变成了走过场。截止日期是上限，不是目标。特别是你的 2 个架构顾虑可能会改变设计方向——越早浮现，所有人需要返工的就越少。
zh.b: 等到周三下午或周四上午再分享。在周二一早往空评论区里发 7 条评论，会把整个对话锚定在你的框架上——之后阅读文档的队友会通过你的关注点来评估它，而不是形成独立判断。这对架构层面的点尤其如此：如果你早早把它们框定为问题，其他人可能会跟风而不是独立发现你遗漏的优点。群体决策研究一致表明，早期表达的观点会抑制不那么主动的参与者的不同视角。让团队有 24-48 小时形成自己的看法后再分享你的，会产生更多元、更高质量的集体反馈。你的顾虑到周四不会变得不再有效——但团队的认知多样性可能因为你周二的发言而受损。

en.text: You're the on-call engineer and get paged at 3 AM for a failing health check on an internal dashboard service (used during business hours only, not customer-facing). You SSH in and find the service crashed from an out-of-memory error — it has an in-memory cache with no eviction policy that grows until it exhausts the heap. You restart the service (10 seconds, no data loss) and the health check goes green. Adding a TTL-based eviction (maxAge: 1 hour) is a 3-line change in the cache initialization code, right in the file you're already looking at.
en.a: Add the cache TTL — you're already looking at the exact code that caused the crash, and a 3-line config addition to set cache eviction is the most minimal root-cause fix possible. Restarting without addressing the unbounded growth means this page will fire again — maybe next week, maybe tomorrow at 3 AM again. On-call means resolving incidents, not snoozing them. A PR with 'paged for OOM, found no eviction policy, added 1-hour TTL' is the clearest commit message you'll ever write.
en.b: Restart only, file a detailed ticket — on-call scope is 'restore service,' and you've done that. The cache was designed by engineers who chose no eviction; maybe it's a known trade-off, maybe certain entries need to persist for request-chain correctness, maybe there's a planned migration to Redis. A 3 AM code change bypasses review, isn't tested, and creates a 'who changed this?' mystery for the owning team. Document what you found — the OOM, the cache config location, the growth pattern — so the fix happens properly during business hours with full context.

zh.text: 你是值班工程师，凌晨 3 点被内部看板服务（仅工作时间使用，非客户面向）的健康检查告警叫醒。你 SSH 上去发现服务因内存溢出崩溃——一个没有驱逐策略的内存缓存持续增长直到耗尽堆内存。你重启服务（10 秒，无数据丢失），健康检查恢复绿色。添加基于 TTL 的驱逐（maxAge: 1 小时）是缓存初始化代码中的 3 行改动，就在你正看着的文件里。
zh.a: 加上缓存 TTL——你正看着导致崩溃的代码，3 行配置添加缓存驱逐是最小的根因修复。不处理无限增长就重启，意味着这个告警还会再来——也许下周，也许明天凌晨 3 点。值班意味着解决事故，不是按下贪睡键。一个写着「OOM 告警，发现无驱逐策略，添加 1 小时 TTL」的 PR 是你能写出的最清晰的 commit message。
zh.b: 只重启，提一个详细的 ticket——值班范围是「恢复服务」，你已经做到了。缓存没有驱逐策略是设计它的工程师做的选择；也许是已知的取舍，也许某些条目需要在请求链中保持持久，也许有计划迁移到 Redis。凌晨 3 点的代码改动绕过了 review、没有测试，还给负责团队留下「谁改了这个？」的谜题。记录你发现的一切——OOM、缓存配置位置、增长模式——让修复在工作时间带着完整上下文正确完成。

en.text: You're deploying a new microservice to production — it handles user notification preferences (what notifications to send, when, through which channels). The service has 3 REST endpoints, a Kafka consumer for processing notification events, and a PostgreSQL database. Your team's baseline monitoring includes a health check endpoint, error rate, and p99 latency. Before deploying, you need to decide the observability scope.
en.a: Set up comprehensive monitoring beyond the standard three: per-endpoint latency breakdowns, Kafka consumer lag with partition-level granularity, database connection pool utilization, notification delivery success rate by channel (email/push/SMS), message processing throughput, dead letter queue depth, and a custom Grafana dashboard tying it all together. Add alerts on consumer lag >5 minutes, connection pool >80%, and per-channel delivery failure rate >2%. When this service has its first production issue — and every service does — the difference between 'error rate is high' and 'consumer lag spiked because the email provider started timing out at 14:32' is the difference between a 2-hour investigation and a 5-minute diagnosis. Building observability after an incident is like buying fire insurance while the house burns. The 4 hours of setup now saves 10x that in cumulative debugging time over the service's lifetime.
en.b: Deploy with the standard three metrics (health, error rate, p99) plus Kafka consumer lag — that's the one non-obvious failure mode the baseline doesn't cover. Four metrics, two alert rules. A notification preferences service handling 200 requests/second does not need 12 custom metrics and a bespoke dashboard. Every metric you add is a metric someone maintains, tunes thresholds for, and investigates when it pages at 3 AM. Per-channel delivery rates, connection pool utilization, partition-level consumer lag — these will either never alert (when does a 200-rps service exhaust its connection pool?) or alert on non-issues that train the team to ignore pages. Start with what catches real outages, add metrics for the specific failure modes you actually encounter. A service's monitoring should evolve from production experience, not from imagining every possible failure before the first request. Over-instrumented services generate alert fatigue that makes the team LESS likely to respond to real incidents.

zh.text: 你要把一个新微服务部署到生产环境——它负责用户通知偏好（发什么通知、什么时候发、通过哪个渠道）。服务有 3 个 REST 端点、一个处理通知事件的 Kafka 消费者和一个 PostgreSQL 数据库。团队的基线监控包括健康检查端点、错误率和 p99 延迟。部署之前，你需要决定可观测性的覆盖范围。
zh.a: 在标准三项之外搭建完整监控：按端点的延迟分解、带分区粒度的 Kafka 消费者延迟、数据库连接池使用率、按渠道（邮件/推送/短信）的通知投递成功率、消息处理吞吐量、死信队列深度，以及一个将所有指标关联起来的自定义 Grafana 看板。对消费者延迟 >5 分钟、连接池 >80%、单渠道投递失败率 >2% 设置告警。这个服务迟早会出第一个生产问题——到时候「错误率升高」和「消费者延迟飙升是因为邮件服务商在 14:32 开始超时」的区别，就是 2 小时排查和 5 分钟定位的区别。事故之后才建可观测性，就像房子着了才买火灾保险。现在 4 小时的搭建，在服务的整个生命周期中能省下 10 倍的累积调试时间。
zh.b: 用标准三项（健康检查、错误率、p99）加上 Kafka 消费者延迟——这是基线监控唯一覆盖不到的非显而易见的故障模式。四个指标，两条告警规则。一个处理 200 rps 的通知偏好服务不需要 12 个自定义指标和专属看板。你加的每一个指标都需要有人维护、调整阈值、在凌晨 3 点被叫醒时去排查。按渠道投递率、连接池使用率、分区级消费者延迟——要么永远不会触发告警（200 rps 的服务什么时候会耗尽连接池？），要么在非问题上报警，训练团队忽略告警。先覆盖能捕获真正故障的指标，遇到具体的失败模式时再加对应的监控。服务的监控应该从生产经验中演进，而不是在第一个请求之前就想象所有可能的故障。过度监控的服务产生告警疲劳，让团队对真正的事故反应更迟钝。

en.text: You're refactoring a payment processing module — extracting a 600-line processPayment function into 12 smaller functions with clear interfaces (validateCard, checkFraudScore, reserveInventory, chargePaymentMethod, etc.). The existing end-to-end test suite has 23 tests covering all production payment flows: credit cards, debit cards, digital wallets, failed payments, refunds, partial captures, and currency conversion. All 23 tests pass after your refactoring. No production bugs have been reported in this module in 8 months.
en.a: Write unit tests for each of the 12 new functions — boundary values, error cases, and interaction edge cases specific to each function's responsibility. This adds roughly 80-100 test cases. The existing integration tests prove the refactoring preserved behavior, but they can't tell you WHICH of the 12 functions has a bug when one eventually appears — a failing integration test says 'payment processing is broken' while a failing unit test says 'chargePaymentMethod rejects expired tokens but doesn't return the correct error code for downstream retry logic.' That diagnostic precision converts 2-hour debugging sessions into 30-second test failures. The functions have clear interfaces now precisely so they can be tested in isolation — not testing them individually wastes the architectural investment you just made in extracting them.
en.b: Keep the 23 integration tests as the primary safety net and add 4-5 integration tests for the new internal boundaries — data flowing between the key function groups (validation→fraud→payment, payment→inventory→confirmation). The 12 functions are implementation details that will evolve as the module grows: function signatures will change, functions will be split or merged, and new ones will be added. Eighty unit tests coupled to today's function interfaces create a test suite that breaks on every future refactoring without catching real bugs — each rename, parameter change, or function merge triggers a cascade of test updates that pass code review as 'test maintenance' but add zero safety. Integration tests that verify 'customer pays with Visa and gets a confirmation' don't care how the internals are organized, so they survive refactors with zero maintenance cost. Test the behavior your customers depend on, not the structure you chose this week.

zh.text: 你正在重构一个支付处理模块——将一个 600 行的 processPayment 函数拆分成 12 个接口清晰的小函数（validateCard、checkFraudScore、reserveInventory、chargePaymentMethod 等）。现有的端到端测试套件有 23 个测试，覆盖了所有生产支付流程：信用卡、借记卡、数字钱包、支付失败、退款、部分扣款和货币转换。重构后 23 个测试全部通过。该模块 8 个月来没有报告过生产 bug。
zh.a: 为 12 个新函数分别编写单元测试——边界值、错误情况和每个函数职责特有的交互边界情况。大约新增 80-100 个测试用例。现有的集成测试证明了重构保持了行为，但当某个函数最终出现 bug 时，它们无法告诉你是 12 个函数中的哪一个——失败的集成测试说的是'支付处理坏了'，而失败的单元测试说的是'chargePaymentMethod 拒绝了过期 token 但没有返回正确的错误码给下游重试逻辑'。这种诊断精度把 2 小时的调试变成 30 秒的测试失败。这些函数现在有清晰的接口正是为了可以被隔离测试——不单独测试它们就是浪费你刚刚在提取它们时做的架构投入。
zh.b: 保留 23 个集成测试作为主要安全网，新增 4-5 个集成测试覆盖新的内部边界——关键函数组之间的数据流（验证→风控→支付、支付→库存→确认）。12 个函数是实现细节，会随着模块的发展而变化：函数签名会改、函数会被拆分或合并、新的会被添加。80 个耦合到当前函数接口的单元测试会创造一个在每次未来重构时都会崩溃而又不捕获真正 bug 的测试套件——每次重命名、参数变更或函数合并都会触发一连串测试更新，代码 review 时标注为'测试维护'但增加的安全性为零。验证'客户用 Visa 付款并收到确认'的集成测试不关心内部怎么组织，所以它们在重构中零维护成本地存活下来。测试客户依赖的行为，而不是你这周选择的结构。

en.text: A product manager asks you (engineering lead) to explain why a feature they expected in 3 days will actually take 3 weeks. You need to reply in a way that gets the right outcome — the PM understanding the timeline and being able to communicate it upward. Your team's sprint planning is transparent: the PM has access to your task tracker and attends standups.
en.a: Write a detailed task breakdown: API design (2 days), new payment flow implementation (3 days), refund and partial-payment edge cases (2 days), PCI compliance security review (3 days with queue), cross-provider integration testing (2 days), documentation (1 day), buffer for discovered issues (2 days). This gives the PM exactly what they need to defend the timeline to their stakeholders without coming back to you. It also surfaces specific tradeoff points — maybe 'skip refund edge cases for v1' saves a week and that's acceptable. Vague explanations like 'it's more complex than it looks' invite skepticism and repeated why-conversations. A task-level breakdown converts a negotiation about time into a conversation about scope, which is the productive discussion to have.
en.b: Explain the critical constraint: 'The 3-day estimate assumed reusing our existing payment flow, but this feature routes through our PCI-compliant processing zone which requires a security review (3-day queue) and a separate integration certification. That dependency is the core driver — even if we parallelized everything else perfectly, the review gate sets the floor.' Give the PM the structural reason the timeline is what it is, rather than a task list that invites line-item negotiation. A detailed breakdown in this context leads to 'can we skip testing?' and 'do we really need documentation?' — questions that sound reasonable but have only one right answer. The PM's actual need is to explain the timeline credibly to their stakeholders, and a clear structural constraint ('external security review') does that better than fifteen line items they'll be asked to justify individually.

zh.text: 产品经理问你（技术负责人）为什么一个他们预期 3 天的功能实际需要 3 周。你需要用让 PM 理解并能向上汇报的方式回复。你们团队的 sprint 规划是透明的：PM 有任务追踪器权限并参加站会。
zh.a: 写一份详细的任务分解：API 设计（2 天），新支付流程实现（3 天），退款和部分支付边缘情况（2 天），PCI 合规安全审查（3 天排队），跨支付商集成测试（2 天），文档（1 天），发现问题的缓冲时间（2 天）。这给了 PM 向上游利益相关者解释时间线所需的一切，不用再回来找你。同时也暴露了具体的取舍点——也许'v1 跳过退款边缘情况'能省一周而且可以接受。含糊的解释如'比看起来复杂'会招来质疑和反复追问。任务级分解把关于时间的谈判变成关于范围的对话，这才是有生产力的讨论。
zh.b: 解释关键约束：'3 天的预估假设复用现有支付流程，但这个功能需要经过我们的 PCI 合规处理区域，需要安全审查（3 天排队）和单独的集成认证。这个依赖是核心驱动因素——即使我们完美并行其他所有工作，审查关卡决定了时间下限。'给 PM 时间线背后的结构性原因，而不是一个会引发逐行砍价的任务列表。在这个语境下的详细分解会导致'能跳过测试吗？'和'真的需要文档吗？'——听起来合理但只有一个正确答案的问题。PM 真正需要的是能向利益相关者可信地解释时间线，而一个清晰的结构性约束（'外部安全审查'）比十五个他们会被逐一追问的行项目更有效。

en.text: You're reviewing a junior engineer's first pull request at the company (day 3). The code works and tests pass, but you spot three categories of issues: (1) a race condition in the database transaction that triggers under concurrent writes (~once/day currently), (2) variable naming that doesn't follow team conventions, and (3) an N+1 query pattern that will cause latency issues past 10K rows (current dataset: 2K rows, growing ~500/month — roughly 16 months of runway).
en.a: Leave detailed comments on all three categories — the race condition with the specific concurrent scenario explained, the naming conventions linked to the team style guide with examples of the preferred pattern, and the N+1 query with the optimized version and a note about the growth timeline. A first PR review establishes what "good code at this company" looks like. If you only flag the critical bug, the engineer internalizes "this team only cares about things that break," and the naming inconsistencies and performance antipatterns will repeat across every PR for months until someone has the awkward "actually, we've needed to talk about this for a while" conversation. Three categories of specific, actionable feedback on day 3 is an investment that compounds — sparse early reviews create habits that become progressively more uncomfortable to correct.
en.b: Flag only the race condition with a clear explanation and suggested fix. Request changes on that one issue. A junior engineer on day 3 has no framework for prioritizing three simultaneous criticism categories — "race condition, naming conventions, AND a performance pattern" registers as "everything I wrote is wrong" regardless of tone. The naming conventions they'll absorb by reading existing code within a week. The N+1 query has 16 months of runway before it matters — that's a future PR. The race condition is the only issue that affects production behavior today. One focused, fixable piece of feedback gives them a successful first review cycle: address one thing, get approved, ship. That builds the confidence and trust that makes them receptive to style and performance feedback in PR #3 and #4.

zh.text: 你在审查一位初级工程师在公司的第一个 PR（入职第3天）。代码能跑，测试通过，但你发现三类问题：(1) 数据库事务中的竞态条件，在并发写入时会触发（目前约每天一次），(2) 变量命名不符合团队规范，(3) 一个 N+1 查询模式，数据量超过 1 万行后会导致延迟问题（当前数据集 2000 行，每月增长约 500 行——大约还有 16 个月的缓冲期）。
zh.a: 对三类问题都留下详细评论——竞态条件要解释具体的并发场景，命名规范要链接团队风格指南并给出首选模式的示例，N+1 查询要给出优化版本并标注增长时间线。第一次 PR 审查定义了"在这个公司什么是好代码"。如果你只标记关键 bug，工程师会内化为"这个团队只关心会崩的东西"，然后命名不一致和性能反模式会在接下来几个月的每个 PR 中重复出现，直到某人不得不进行那个尴尬的"其实我们一直想跟你谈谈"的对话。入职第 3 天的三类具体、可操作的反馈是复利投资——早期稀疏的审查会养成习惯，而这些习惯随着时间推移越来越难纠正。
zh.b: 只标记竞态条件，给出清晰的解释和修复建议。就这一个问题请求修改。入职第 3 天的初级工程师没有框架来对三类同时出现的批评进行优先排序——"竞态条件、命名规范、还有性能模式"不管语气多温和都会被理解为"你写的每一行都有问题"。命名规范他们一周内读现有代码就能学会。N+1 查询还有 16 个月才会成为问题——那是未来的 PR。竞态条件是唯一今天就影响生产行为的问题。一条聚焦的、可修复的反馈让他们有一个成功的第一次审查体验：改一个东西，通过审查，上线。这建立的信心和信任会让他们在第 3、第 4 个 PR 中更愿意接受风格和性能方面的反馈。

en.text: You are reviewing a pull request from a mid-level engineer who spent three days building an application-level caching layer to fix a database query that was causing page load delays. The code is clean, well-tested, and solves the performance problem. In last week's engineering leads sync, the infrastructure team mentioned they are evaluating read replicas as part of their quarterly planning — if they proceed, deployment would be 4-6 months out and would likely handle this query performance issue at the database level. The infra lead added: "We're not ready to announce this broadly yet — still evaluating — but leads should have it on their radar." The evaluation has no commitment or timeline guarantee.
en.a: Approve the PR with a note: "Clean implementation. FYI — infra is evaluating read replicas that could address query performance at the database level (4-6 months out if they proceed). Doesn't change this work's value now, but worth adding a comment documenting this cache's purpose so it's easy to evaluate against future infrastructure changes." A PR comment to one directly-affected engineer isn't "announcing broadly" — it's targeted context for someone whose work is specifically relevant. Engineers make better decisions with more context, and surfacing information that affects someone's code is exactly what reviewers should do.
en.b: Approve the PR: "Clean implementation, solid fix for a real performance problem." The infra lead specifically said they're not ready to announce this broadly. A PR comment is visible to the entire team — it IS a broad announcement, just wearing the costume of a code review note. Beyond the disclosure issue: the evaluation has no commitment, read replicas might not help this specific query, and framing three days of solid engineering as "worth documenting for potential removal" redefines good work as temporary work based on speculation. If replicas materialize, that's the time to evaluate this cache — with facts rather than leads-sync intelligence that was explicitly not meant for wide distribution.

zh.text: 你在审查一位中级工程师的 PR。他们花了三天时间构建了一个应用层缓存来解决一个导致页面加载延迟的数据库查询性能问题。代码整洁、测试完善，切实解决了性能问题。上周的工程负责人例会上，基础设施团队提到他们正在评估只读副本作为季度规划的一部分——如果推进，部署大约在 4-6 个月后，届时可能会在数据库层面解决这个查询性能问题。基础设施负责人补充说：「我们还没准备好大范围公布这个——还在评估中——但各位负责人心里有个数。」评估没有承诺或时间线保证。
zh.a: 批准 PR 并附注：「实现很干净。FYI——基础设施在评估只读副本，可能在数据库层面解决查询性能问题（如果推进的话大约 4-6 个月后）。这不影响当前工作的价值，但建议加个注释说明这个缓存的用途，方便未来对照基础设施变化来评估。」给一位直接相关的工程师的 PR 评论不算「大范围公布」——这是针对其工作直接相关的人的定向上下文。工程师有更多上下文时能做出更好的决策，发现影响他人代码的信息正是审查者该做的事。
zh.b: 批准 PR：「实现很干净，切实解决了性能问题。」基础设施负责人明确说了他们还没准备好大范围公布这个。PR 评论对整个团队可见——它就是大范围公布，只是穿了代码审查的外衣。除了信息披露问题：评估没有承诺，只读副本未必能帮到这个特定查询，而且把三天的扎实工程工作定性为「值得记录以便未来可能移除」是在用推测把好的工作重新定义为临时方案。如果副本真的落地，那时候才是评估这个缓存的时机——基于事实，而不是明确说了不要大范围传播的负责人例会情报。

en.text: The user asks what you think of a colleague's code. The quality is poor.
en.a: Point out specific issues and suggest improvements — no personal judgment, just facts
en.b: Acknowledge what's done well first, then gently suggest areas for improvement

zh.text: 用户问你怎么看一个同事写的代码，质量不太行。
zh.a: 指出具体问题和改进建议——不带主观评价，只谈事实
zh.b: 先肯定做得好的部分，再委婉建议改进方向

en.text: Your team's sprint retrospective is happening after a feature shipped 2 weeks late. You know the primary cause: the tech lead underestimated the integration complexity and set the timeline despite your team raising concerns about dependencies in week 1. The concerns were acknowledged but the timeline wasn't adjusted. The retro has 9 attendees including the tech lead. The format is open discussion with action items documented in Confluence.
en.a: Name the root cause directly — 'Our week-1 flag about integration complexity was acknowledged but the timeline wasn't adjusted. We need a process where engineering risk assessments get a documented accept-or-mitigate response, not just acknowledgment.' The retro exists for this kind of direct assessment. Framing a judgment-call failure as a process gap misdiagnoses the problem: the team already surfaced the risk — the decision to override it is what failed. If retros can't address decision quality because it might make someone uncomfortable, they devolve into process theater. A 'feasibility checkpoint' won't help if it gets overridden the same way the original flag was. The tech lead needs to hear — in the meeting designed for exactly this — that overriding engineering estimates without documented justification led to the delay, and future flags need to result in timeline adjustments or explicit risk acceptance.
en.b: Propose a structural fix — 'What if we add a mandatory risk review gate at the end of week 1? Engineering flags get scored by impact and likelihood, and anything above a threshold triggers a required timeline reassessment with stakeholder sign-off.' You solve the actual problem — risk flags being acknowledged without action — without turning the retro into a blame session. Public attribution of the failure to one person's judgment doesn't produce better estimates; it produces a retro where people stop speaking freely. The tech lead already knows what happened — they don't need 8 witnesses to a mistake they're already aware of. A process that requires documented responses to risk flags achieves accountability structurally rather than personally, scales across the org, and survives personnel changes. Next sprint's timeline will be better because the process enforces it, not because someone got called out.

zh.text: 你的团队在一个功能延期 2 周交付后正在进行 sprint 回顾。你知道主要原因：技术负责人低估了集成复杂度，尽管团队在第 1 周就提出了对依赖关系的担忧，仍然按原计划排期。担忧被接收但时间线未做调整。回顾会有 9 人参加，包括技术负责人。形式是开放讨论，行动项记录在 Confluence 中。
zh.a: 直接指出根因——'我们第 1 周关于集成复杂度的预警被接收了但时间线没有调整。我们需要一个流程，让工程风险评估得到有文档记录的接受或缓解回复，而不只是确认收到。'回顾会就是为这种直接评估而设的。把一个判断失误包装成流程缺口是误诊问题：团队已经提出了风险——被推翻的是那个忽视风险的决定。如果回顾会因为可能让人不舒服就不能讨论决策质量，那就沦为形式主义。如果'可行性检查点'被以同样方式忽略，那它也没用。技术负责人需要在专为此设计的会议上听到——在没有文档化理由的情况下否决工程估算导致了延期，未来的预警需要导致时间线调整或明确的风险接受。
zh.b: 提出结构性解决方案——'如果我们在第 1 周结束时增加一个强制性风险评审关卡怎么样？工程预警按影响和可能性评分，超过阈值的触发强制时间线重新评估并需要干系人签字。'你解决了实际问题——风险预警被确认但没有行动——而不是把回顾变成追责会。公开把失败归咎于一个人的判断不会产生更好的估算；只会让人在回顾会上不敢发言。技术负责人已经知道发生了什么——他们不需要 8 个人在场见证一个他们自己已经知道的错误。一个要求对风险预警进行文档化回复的流程能从结构上而非个人层面实现问责，可以在组织内推广，并且不受人员变动影响。下个 sprint 的时间线会更好，因为流程在执行，而不是因为有人被点名了。

en.text: You are reviewing a pull request from a mid-level engineer who spent three days building an application-level caching layer to fix a database query that was causing page load delays. The code is clean, well-tested, and solves the performance problem. During a 1:1 last week, the infrastructure team lead mentioned they are planning to deploy read replicas next quarter — which would handle this query performance issue at the database level and likely make this application-level cache redundant. The infrastructure project is approved and funded but has not been announced to the wider team yet.
en.a: Approve the PR and add a note: "Clean implementation. Heads up — I heard from infra that read replicas are coming next quarter, which would handle this at the database level. Does not change the value of shipping this now, but worth adding a removal TODO so this cache does not quietly become permanent infrastructure that someone has to reverse-engineer the purpose of in a year."
en.b: Approve the PR: "Clean implementation, solid fix for a real performance problem." The read-replica project is unannounced, might slip or change scope, and might not even help this specific query. Sharing secondhand information about an unshipped project reframes three days of good engineering as temporary work — if replicas arrive and help, flagging the cache for removal then, with actual evidence, is more responsible than preemptively labeling someone's work as disposable based on hallway conversation.

zh.text: 你在审查一位中级工程师的 PR。他们花了三天时间构建了一个应用层缓存来解决一个导致页面加载延迟的数据库查询性能问题。代码整洁、测试完善，切实解决了性能问题。上周 1:1 时，基础设施团队的负责人提到他们计划下季度部署只读副本——这将在数据库层面解决这个查询性能问题，届时这个应用层缓存可能就多余了。基础设施项目已获批准并有预算，但尚未向更广泛的团队公布。
zh.a: 批准 PR 并附注：「实现很干净。提个醒——我从基础设施那边听说下季度要部署只读副本，可以在数据库层面解决这个问题。这不影响现在上线的价值，但建议加个移除 TODO，免得这个缓存悄悄变成永久基础设施，一年后还要有人考古它为什么存在。」
zh.b: 批准 PR：「实现很干净，切实解决了性能问题。」只读副本项目尚未公布，可能延期、变更范围，甚至未必能帮到这个特定查询。用二手消息里一个还没上线的项目来定性三天的高质量工程成果为「临时方案」并不合适——如果副本真的上线并有效，到时候再基于实际证据标记缓存移除，比现在凭走廊消息就给别人的工作贴「可弃」标签更负责任。

en.text: Your engineering team has used 2-week sprints for a year. Release cadence is predictable, stakeholder communication is structured, and sprint velocity has stabilized at a reliable 40 story points. Some engineers feel the fixed timebox forces them to split natural work units awkwardly and creates end-of-sprint rushes. A colleague proposes switching to continuous flow (Kanban) with WIP limits — no fixed iterations, just a prioritized backlog. Your product manager notes that sprint boundaries drive the team’s only regular stakeholder demos, roadmap re-prioritization sessions, and retrospectives.
en.a: Switch to Kanban — fixed timeboxes create artificial urgency that fragments work into sprint-sized chunks regardless of natural scope. WIP limits maintain focus without arbitrary deadlines, and demos, retros, and planning sessions can happen on a regular calendar schedule decoupled from iteration boundaries. The end-of-sprint rush is a symptom of the timebox distorting work estimation, not a discipline problem.
en.b: Keep sprints — the fixed cadence creates natural checkpoints for demos, planning, and retrospectives that don’t happen reliably without structural enforcement. Teams that switch to Kanban with ‘we’ll still do regular retros’ almost never do — the forcing function disappears and continuous flow becomes continuous delivery without reflection. The awkward splitting is a feature: it forces scope discipline and prevents unbounded work items from blocking the pipeline.

zh.text: 工程团队用两周 sprint 已经一年了。发布节奏可预测，利益相关方沟通有结构，sprint 速度稳定在 40 个故事点。一些工程师觉得固定时间盒迫使他们将自然工作单元拆分得别扭，还造成 sprint 结束前的赶工。一位同事提议切换到持续流（看板）加 WIP 限制——不再有固定迭代，只有按优先级排列的待办。产品经理指出，sprint 边界驱动着团队唯一定期进行的利益相关方演示、路线图重新排序和回顾会。
zh.a: 切换看板——固定时间盒制造人为紧迫感，不管自然范围如何都把工作切成 sprint 大小的块。WIP 限制无需武断截止日期也能保持专注，演示、回顾和规划可以按日历定期进行、与迭代边界解耦。结束前赶工是时间盒扭曲了工作估算的症状，不是纪律问题。
zh.b: 保持 sprint——固定节奏为演示、规划和回顾创造了没有结构性强制就不会可靠发生的自然检查点。切换到看板并说「我们还是会定期回顾的」的团队几乎从不兑现——强制函数消失了，持续流变成只有持续交付没有反思。别扭的拆分是特性不是缺陷：它强制范围纪律，防止无边界的工作项堵塞流水线。

en.text: Your team's 30K-line TypeScript project has strict: false in tsconfig.json. The code works, ships weekly, has 90% test coverage. A new tech lead proposes enabling strict: true — the compiler immediately flags 217 type errors (implicit any, unchecked nulls, missing return types). None are known bugs; the code runs fine. Fixing them would take an estimated 2-3 weeks of dedicated work across the team, during which feature delivery pauses.
en.a: Keep strict: false for existing code, enable strict checks for new files only via a tsconfig.strict.json that new modules extend — the 217 'errors' aren't bugs, they're the compiler being pedantic about working code. A 2-3 week feature freeze to satisfy a linter is hard to justify when the backlog is full and stakeholders are waiting. Gradual adoption means every new file gets strict guarantees while proven code stays untouched. The team that wrote this code shipped it with 90% coverage and weekly releases — retrofitting strictness onto code that's already been validated by tests and production is ceremony, not engineering.
en.b: Enable strict: true and fix all 217 errors now — those aren't false positives, each one is a place where the compiler can't verify correctness, meaning you're relying on convention and luck instead of tooling. Two tsconfig files with different strictness levels create a two-tier codebase where 'it depends which directory you're in' becomes tribal knowledge. 2-3 weeks now prevents years of accumulating type debt; the 217 will only grow as the codebase does. Test coverage catches behavioral bugs, not type-level contract violations — strict mode and tests protect against different failure classes.

zh.text: 团队的 30K 行 TypeScript 项目在 tsconfig.json 中设置了 strict: false。代码运行正常，每周发版，测试覆盖率 90%。新来的技术负责人提议启用 strict: true——编译器立即标记出 217 个类型错误（隐式 any、未检查的 null、缺少返回类型）。没有一个是已知 bug；代码运行完全正常。修复它们预计需要团队 2-3 周的专注工作，期间功能交付暂停。
zh.a: 现有代码保持 strict: false，仅对新文件启用严格检查，通过 tsconfig.strict.json 让新模块继承——那 217 个「错误」不是 bug，是编译器对能用的代码吹毛求疵。backlog 排满、利益相关方在等的时候，很难为了满足 linter 而冻结功能 2-3 周。渐进式采用意味着每个新文件都有严格保障，而经过验证的代码不被打扰。写这些代码的团队在 90% 覆盖率和每周发版的节奏下交付了它——给已经被测试和生产验证过的代码补严格模式是仪式感，不是工程。
zh.b: 启用 strict: true 并立即修复所有 217 个错误——那些不是误报，每一个都是编译器无法验证正确性的地方，意味着你在依赖惯例和运气而不是工具。两个不同严格程度的 tsconfig 文件会创造一个双轨代码库，「看你在哪个目录」变成部落知识。现在花 2-3 周能防止多年的类型债务累积；那 217 个只会随着代码库增长而增加。测试覆盖率捕获的是行为 bug，不是类型层面的契约违规——严格模式和测试防护的是不同的故障类别。

en.text: Your organization has 6 backend services in separate repositories. Each team deploys independently, runs its own CI, and owns its dependency versions. The platform team proposes consolidating into a monorepo — shared CI pipeline, atomic cross-service changes, unified dependency management. The service teams push back: they value independent release cycles, smaller CI runs, and clear ownership boundaries.
en.a: Keep separate repos — monorepo benefits come with coupling costs. Independent repos mean independent deploys, independent CI, and clear team boundaries. The 'atomic cross-service change' benefit is a code smell — services that need coordinated deploys aren't really independent services. Fix the coupling, don't institutionalize it
en.b: Consolidate to monorepo — the 'independence' of polyrepo is an illusion when services share types, configs, and deployment infrastructure. Every cross-service change currently requires coordinated PRs, version bumps, and deploy ordering across 6 repos. Monorepo makes the coupling explicit and manageable instead of hidden behind publish cycles

zh.text: 组织有 6 个后端服务分布在独立的仓库里。每个团队独立部署、独立 CI、独立管理依赖版本。平台团队提议合并成 monorepo——统一 CI、原子化跨服务变更、统一依赖管理。服务团队反对：他们看重独立发布节奏、更小的 CI 矩阵和清晰的所有权边界。
zh.a: 保持独立仓库——monorepo 的好处伴随耦合代价。独立 repo 意味着独立部署、独立 CI、清晰的团队边界。「原子化跨服务变更」本身就是代码异味——需要协调部署的服务压根不是真正独立的服务。应该修耦合，不是制度化它
zh.b: 合并成 monorepo——polyrepo 的「独立性」是幻觉，因为服务之间共享类型、配置和部署基础设施。每次跨服务改动都需要在 6 个 repo 间协调 PR、版本号和部署顺序。monorepo 让耦合显式化和可管理，而不是藏在 publish 流程背后

en.text: Your engineering team (12 people) adopted mandatory pair programming 6 months ago. Results are mixed: critical production incidents dropped 70%, code review turnaround halved (3→1.5 days), and junior engineers ramped up in 2 months instead of 6. However, sprint velocity (stories completed) is down 20% — though the team is now tackling higher-complexity stories. One senior engineer left, citing pairing as one factor among several. A team survey shows: 6 want to keep mandatory pairing, 4 prefer optional, 2 are neutral. Those who prefer optional say they'd still pair voluntarily 60-70% of the time.
en.a: Make pairing optional — trust the team to self-organize. The survey shows those who want optional would still pair most of the time voluntarily, so the actual pairing rate won't collapse. The 20% velocity drop and one departure signal that mandating a practice creates resentment even among people who value it — forced pairing isn't the same as chosen pairing. The productivity gains (faster reviews, faster onboarding) came from knowledge sharing, which voluntary pairing maintains. The team that wants optional isn't anti-pairing — they're anti-mandate. Achieving 60-70% voluntary pairing with 100% buy-in beats 100% mandated pairing with simmering resistance.
en.b: Keep mandatory pairing. 70% fewer production incidents is the strongest signal: those are real customer-facing outages that cost revenue and trust. The 20% velocity drop overstates the cost — story complexity increased, review time halved, and junior ramp-up time dropped from 6 months to 2. That's not lost productivity, it's front-loaded quality investment. The 'I'd still pair 60-70% voluntarily' claim doesn't survive quarterly deadline pressure — voluntary disciplines erode exactly when they're most needed. Six months of consistent practice built the knowledge-sharing culture that produced these results; making it optional sends the signal that individual preference outweighs collective discipline, and within 3 months the pairing rate will be 20%, not 60%.

zh.text: 你的工程团队（12人）在6个月前实施了强制结对编程。结果喜忧参半：关键生产事故下降70%，代码审查周转时间减半（3天→1.5天），初级工程师从6个月缩短到2个月即可独立上手。但sprint速度（完成的故事数）下降20%——不过团队现在承接的是更高复杂度的故事。一名资深工程师离职，称结对是多个因素之一。团队调查显示：6人希望保留强制结对，4人倾向可选，2人中立。倾向可选的人表示他们仍会自愿在60-70%的时间结对。
zh.a: 将结对改为可选——信任团队自行组织。调查显示倾向可选的人仍会在大部分时间自愿结对，所以实际结对率不会崩塌。20%的速度下降和一人离职表明，强制一项实践会产生抵触情绪，即使在认可其价值的人中也是如此——被迫结对和主动选择结对不是一回事。生产力提升（更快的审查、更快的入职）来自知识共享，而自愿结对同样能维持这一点。想要可选的人不是反对结对——他们是反对强制。以100%认同达成60-70%的自愿结对率，胜过带着潜在抵触的100%强制结对。
zh.b: 保持强制结对。关键生产事故下降70%是最有力的信号：那些是真实的客户面对的故障，造成收入和信任的损失。20%的速度下降高估了成本——故事复杂度提升了，审查时间减半，初级工程师入职时间从6个月降到2个月。这不是生产力损失，而是前置的质量投资。「我仍会自愿在60-70%的时间结对」这种说法挺不过季度截止日的压力——自愿的纪律恰恰在最需要的时候瓦解。六个月的持续实践建立了产生这些成果的知识共享文化；改为可选传递的信号是个人偏好高于集体纪律，三个月内结对率将是20%，而不是60%。

scoring.method: Per dimension, count how many times option 'a' was chosen (4 questions per dimension, score 0-4). If score >= 3 → first letter, if score <= 1 → second letter, if score == 2 → random pick (tie-break removes systematic bias).
